title: Perfect complexes have a set of representatives
statement: For every quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X [def-pc-scheme], the full subcategory of perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-complex] in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] has a set of representatives up to isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh, set-of-representatives input for perfect complexes

proof.text: Use P(U)=PerfectComplexClassesSmallOnOpen X U. If U is affine and an open immersion f:Y into X has image U, the equal-range isomorphism Y ≅ U.toScheme makes Y affine. Apply the affine smallness theorem for every derived-category structure on Y. This proves P on affine opens.

For U quasi-compact and V affine use the gluing smallness implication with P(U),P(V),P(U intersect V). Apply quasiCompactOpen_induction to get P(top), then evaluate at the identity open immersion of X and its given derived-category structures.

Let Q be the property IsPerfect on D_QCoh(X). Shrink Skeleton(Q.FullSubcategory) to Type u. For each shrunk class use fromSkeleton to get a perfect quasi-coherent representative and forget Q. For each E with proof of perfectness, use its skeleton class as the index. The equivShrink inverse identity and fromSkeletonToSkeletonIso give an isomorphism in the perfect full subcategory; mapping by Q.ι gives E ≅ P i in D_QCoh(X). This constructs all clauses of the original existential statement.

proof_origin.place: Original affine/Mayer-Vietoris/08DR route, reduced to affine and gluing smallness; skeleton-to-representatives combination formalized by X2

split_report.summary: Repaired the false chain-level encoding argument. The proof now uses the affine derived equivalence together with Stacks 08CM/08EB for the affine set of classes, then the derived Mayer–Vietoris triangle (08BV) to reduce a two-open gluing step to sets of restrictions and Hom-sets, and finally the existing qcqs induction principle.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the set-of-representatives clause of Theorem perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh.

tool_uses.why: The affine derived equivalence is a generic tool from the Picard-f-representable unit needed to identify affine perfect objects with bounded finite-projective complexes.
Its statement is the generic qcqs induction principle applied to the property P(W) of having a set of perfect-object isomorphism classes; no node in this unit restates that induction principle.
